items.title: Incoming Mississauga mayor pushes for provincial funding during first Queen's Park visit
items.summary: During his first visit to Queen's Park since being elected mayor of Mississauga, Alvin Tedjo says he's pushing for more financial support from the province to help him address some key priorities.

items.title: International competition in Toronto will hear life story of Mississauga woman
items.summary: Karen Craggs is getting ready to tell the story of her life in front of a Toronto audience, and she could walk away the winner of a prestigious speaking competition for doing so. Described in professional circles as an inclusive leadership expert, keynote speaker and organizational excellence strategist, the Mississauga woman is one of 14 finalists who’ll compete on Nov. 21 to become Speaker Slam’s Inspirational Speaker of the Year. The 10th annual Grand Slam Inspirational Speaking Final takes place at CBC Glenn Gould Studio in Toronto and is the culmination of North America’s largest such annual competition. Speaker Slam is a Toronto-based inspirational speaking competition that draws entries from across North America and around the world. Competitors take to the stage at qualifying tournaments throughout the year leading up to the November finals. “The strongest speakers from every qualifier return for one night at CBC Glenn Gould Studio in Toronto,” competition organizers said, adding this year’s theme is Catalyst: what changed you, and how that change made you someone who changes things for others. In addition to being named Speaker Slam’s Inspirational Speaker of the Year, the winner will also receive $5,000 in cash and a prize package valued at up to $50,000. Speaker Slam co-founder Dan Shaikh said in a news release that this year’s theme — Catalyst: what changed you, and how that change made you someone who changes things for others — describes Craggs’ life’s work. He noted Craggs is well known as an inclusive leadership expert, a style of leadership and management that focuses on valuing and empowering diverse team members.

items.title: Questions surround future of historic restaurant in Mississauga
items.summary: The Franklin House, a longtime restaurant and bar housed in one of Mississauga’s most historic buildings, is currently closed, leaving residents wondering what will happen to the landmark establishment. There are indications the Streetsville business could soon reopen under new ownership, with Mississauga Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt saying he has heard a new operator is preparing to take over and could welcome customers soon. The sudden closure has prompted considerable discussion in Streetsville, but the details surrounding the change remain unclear. com. ” However, Butt stressed that he has not been contacted directly by anyone involved in the business and does not know whether it will retain its familiar name or restaurant format. “Whether they just continue to run it exactly how it’s been run before, or whether there’s going to be some change to the format, I don’t know,” he said. Butt also pointed to some of the challenges associated with operating a restaurant in the historic building, including its relatively small main-floor dining area and limited space upstairs. He said the upper floor is better suited to occasional private functions than regular restaurant operations, while the basement presents another potential challenge because of flooding.

items.title: This Mississauga lottery player was once happy to win $500. His 2nd win is 'more exciting'
items.summary: The winning ticket was purchased at Petro-Canada on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga. Corey John of Mississauga wins an Encore prize of $100,000 in the Sept. 19 Lotto 6-49 draw. A Mississauga man who has been playing the lottery regularly for about a decade has won his first major prize. Corey John won an Encore prize of $100,000 in the Sept. 19 Lotto 6-49 draw. “My biggest win before this was $500,” he said in an Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corp. news release. ” He said when he shared the news with his fiancée, she didn’t believe him at first. “I think a vacation is coming up. Maybe a little renovation to the house too,” he said of his plans for the winnings. The winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada gas station on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga.

items.title: Dedicated lottery player from Mississauga wins big after 10 years
items.summary: Mississauga’s Corey J. appears to be one for understatement if his reaction to a big lottery win is any indication. The Mississauga man, a loyal lottery player with OLG for the past decade, is $100,000 richer after the last six of seven Encore numbers on his Sept. 19 Lotto 6/49 ticket matched in exact order the winning numbers for that draw. His previous biggest win playing the lottery was $500, he told Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation (OLG) officials while picking up his cheque. “I was happy with that one, but this one’s a little more exciting,” Corey said recently, in understated fashion, while at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto to collect his windfall. Reflecting on the moment he discovered his big win, Corey, who plays Lotto 6/49 twice weekly and always adds Encore, said it was completely unexpected. “I was definitely surprised. I told my fiancée, and she didn’t believe me at first,” he said. Now $100,000 wealthier, the Mississauga winner said he has some definite plans for the money. “I think a vacation is coming up. Maybe a little renovation to the house, too,” he told OLG officials.

items.title: Food World Plus opens in Mississauga as Ontario’s largest grocery store
items.summary: Grocery shopping just got a whole lot bigger. Ontario’s largest grocery store has officially opened its doors in Mississauga, bringing flavours, ingredients and cuisines from countries and regions around the world under one roof. Food World Plus opened to shoppers on Oct. 30, welcoming residents from across the GTA to explore its massive 176,000-square-foot facility at 50 Matheson Blvd. East. The grocery store has made global food its main selling point, highlighting products and ingredients from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. With such a wide range of international offerings, the store is looking to cater to Mississauga’s diverse population while giving shoppers access to ingredients they might otherwise have to visit multiple specialty grocery stores to find. Beyond its international food selection, Food World Plus is also positioning itself as a one-stop shopping destination, with a range of departments including a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and in-house butcher. Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo was in attendance for the store’s grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford. Tedjo later took to social media to welcome the new addition to the city. “Food World Plus has everything you need and more! ” Tedjo said in an Instagram post. One of the store’s standout offerings is its dedicated halal section within the meat department. According to Food World Plus, the meat is sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards, from delivery to the cuts prepared for customers.

items.title: Busy beavers cause water flow problems in Mississauga and refuse to leave
items.summary: There’s a battle with beavers going on in Mississauga’s north end — and the beavers are winning. Last fall and over the winter, the City of Mississauga removed a number of beaver dams and beavers from in and around Sixteen Mile Creek and Osprey Marsh in the heart of the Lisgar community in the northwest part of the city near the Milton border. The critters, who were safely relocated, had built dams that were causing drainage problems near the creek and marsh. That subsequently led to water flow problems, the city said. Not so fast. Residents reported to Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden, who represents the area, that they’d spotted the beavers back in town this past spring. The reported sightings prompted McFadden to declare she and City of Mississauga staff were going to keep a close eye on the situation as they searched for a better solution. “Additional attention is being paid to this matter in the coming weeks,” the councillor told constituents at the time. Aerial image shows location of Osprey Marsh and surrounding neighbourhoods. Fast-forward to earlier this week when McFadden told residents in her latest update that beavers, among the largest living rodents in the world, “continue to reside along the Sixteen Mile Creek running through Lisgar.

items.title: Buyer-Friendly Market Pushes Mississauga's Lowest October Home Sale to $265,000
items.summary: Zoocasa says the least expensive home sold in Mississauga last month went for $265,000, as buyer-friendly market conditions pull some sale prices well under $300,000 across the Greater Toronto Area. According to the real estate brokerage, the city's average home price dipped 5 per cent month-over-month to $929,600 in September, though that figure remains below the $969,501 average recorded in September 2025, per Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. Zoocasa said the most affordable sales are typically condo units going for under $500,000. Among the five cheapest homes sold in October, the brokerage listed a two-bedroom corner unit in the new M City development, which has floor-to-ceiling windows, a wrap-around balcony and building amenities including a skating rink and rooftop terrace, selling for $432,000 over its $399,000 asking price. Another listed sale was a one-bedroom-plus-den suite in City Centre with more than 700 square feet of space, nine-foot ceilings and access to indoor and outdoor pools, a fitness centre and 24-hour concierge service.

items.title: Peel Region's New AI Assistant Answers Resident Questions Around the Clock in More Than 30 Languages
items.summary: Peel Region says residents in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon can now get help with regional services at any hour through an artificial-intelligence-powered virtual assistant introduced in August. According to the region, the tool goes beyond pointing users to webpages, letting them ask questions in everyday language and have more detailed conversations about complicated requests. The assistant remembers context during a conversation, the region said, so residents don't need to repeatedly explain what they're looking for. It operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and supports more than 30 languages, including English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Arabic, Hindi and Chinese. Peel said one of its most practical uses is helping residents navigate the region's online account system, which covers services such as the Affordable Transit Program, Peel Living and water bill payments. The region added that an online account also lets residents track service requests and applications without having to visit a municipal office in person. Officials said the assistant is part of the broader Digital Peel initiative aimed at making government services more accessible.

items.title: Peel Police Warn Bystander Photos of Tactical Officers Put Lives at Risk During UTM Standoff
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say officers were put at risk after bystanders posted real-time photos and videos of their tactical positions during Monday night's armed standoff at the University of Toronto Mississauga. According to Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, who addressed reporters Tuesday at the UTM campus, a 19-year-old man armed with a gun had barricaded himself inside a student residence and did not respond to negotiators for several hours before officers found him dead of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. Police said various images showing officers' tactical positions began appearing on social media as the operation unfolded. Bell-Morena said posting that kind of real-time detail is a blatant safety concern that puts officers in harm's way and could jeopardize the safety of any victims or hostages inside. He added that, fortunately, there were no hostages in this case. Police are asking the public not to share live images or video of officers responding to situations where lives could be at risk.

items.title: Dundas Street East Lanes Shut After Motorcyclist Hurt in Early-Morning Mississauga Crash
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a motorcyclist was seriously injured in a crash involving a vehicle and a motorcycle early Wednesday morning in Mississauga. According to police, the collision happened at Dundas Street East and Haines Road, and the motorcycle rider was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Police said the eastbound lanes of Dundas Street East are closed at Haines Road, with one westbound lane also shut down. Officers added that Haines Road is closed to northbound traffic south of Dundas Street East while the investigation continues. Police are advising drivers travelling through the area to expect delays until the roads reopen.
